activity_context.topic_title: Determining Characteristics of Moving Objects Using Integration

feedback.problem: A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with acceleration, measured in $\text{m}/{\text{s}}^{2},$ given by the function $a(t)=3{t}^{2}-6t-4,$ where $t>0$ is the time in seconds.  The positive direction is left to right. If the particle is stationary when $t=4\,\text{s},$ determine the time intervals in which the particle moves to the left.
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we find $v(t)$ by integrating the acceleration with respect to time:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\text{d}t \\  & =\int (3{t}^{2}-6t-4)\text{d}t \\  & ={t}^{3}-3{t}^{2}-4t+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C,$ we use the fact that $v(0)=0.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}0 & =(4)^{3}-3(4)^{2}-4(4)+C \\ C & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the velocity $v$ of the particle at time $t$ is $v(t)={t}^{3}-3{t}^{2}-4t.$

To find the time interval in which the particle is moving to the *left*, we must solve the inequality $v<0.$ This gives

$$
{t}^{3}-3{t}^{2}-4t=t(t-4)(t+1)<0.
$$

Plotting the graph of $v(t)$, we get the following picture.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14094076/assets/002f547b882940d087d6ed9d228334ec163931cfea0665eafdfe8b6ec8d863da.png)

From the graph, we see that $v<0$ whenever $0<t<4.$
